channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: China’s June Trade Balance: Surplus widens sharply amid strong exports
item.description: China's Trade Balance for June, in Chinese Yuan (CNY) terms, arrives at CNY859.05 billion, widening from the previous figure of CNY723.98 billion.

item.title: British Pound strengthens above 1.3350 ahead of US CPI data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades in positive territory around 1.3360 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. However, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid fears of an escalating US-Iran conflict.

item.title: US CENTCOM says US forces complete new strikes on Iranian military targets
item.description: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) said on Tuesday that US forces complete new strikes on Iranian military targets, adding that more than 50,000 US service members are currently deployed across the Middle East, Reuters reported.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD dips as oil surge lifts Fed hike odds
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) loses ground for the third consecutive day, trading around $57.60 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Iran’s IRGC says cooperation with 'aggressor enemy' in Hormuz will delay reopening of waterway
item.description: The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said on Tuesday that two 'offending supertankers' were hit and disabled in the Strait of Hormuz. IRGC said that tankers ignored warnings, turned off navigation systems and tried to pass through 'mined route.’

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates as USD bulls look to US CPI and Fed's Warsh
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is seen consolidating the previous day's strong move up and trading just below mid-162.00s during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Sharp shift in asset management environment could prompt review of GPIF portfolio
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Tuesday that the government may consider a pension asset allocation tweak if the environment changes.

item.title: Euro posts modest gains above 1.1350 as traders await US CPI inflation release
item.description: The EUR/USD pair posts modest gains near 1.1385 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. Nonetheless, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid renewed US military strikes against Iran.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains on higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD continues its losing streak after remaining flat in the previous day, trading around 1.4150 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair depreciates as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) receives support from higher oil prices.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rallies as RBNZ's Conway fuels rate hike bets
item.description: The NZD/USD pair attracts some dip-buyers during the Asian session on Tuesday, stalling the previous day's retracement slide from the vicinity of the 0.5800 mark or the monthly peak touched last week.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7990 vs. 6.7972 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7990 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7972 and 6.7927 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI spikes amid escalating Middle East Tensions
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around $79.60 per barrel during the Asian hours on Tuesday. Crude oil prices rise due to mounting supply anxieties following a sharp escalation of geopolitical hostilities in the Middle East.

item.title: Australian Dollar weakens to near 0.6900 as US launches more strikes against Iran
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades with mild losses around 0.6915 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. Ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to boost a safe-haven currency such as the US Dollar (USD) against the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: Iranian missiles hit two UAE tankers in Hormuz — Reuters
item.description: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) Ministry of Defence said that two UAE national tankers, the Mombasa and Al Bahiyah, were targeted by two Iranian cruise missiles in the southern lane of the Strait of Hormuz, in Omani territorial waters, Reuters reported on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold tumbles below $4,000 on Trump’s Iran port blockade move, US CPI data looms
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) remains under selling pressure near $3,995 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal extends its downside as renewed US-Iran tensions keep inflationary pressures high.

item.title: RBNZ's Conway: Inflation to return to 2% over medium term
item.description: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Chief Economist Paul Conway said on Tuesday that the central bank is not discussing a shift to a tightened policy stance, adding that inflation is to return to 2% over the medium term.

item.title: China: Prolonged stagnation path – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao argues China’s housing downturn, now in its fifth year, is settling into an L-shaped stagnation with a pronounced K-shaped regional divergence.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Johor result keeps policy continuity – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Barisan Nasional’s strong win in Johor reinforces UMNO’s political momentum but leaves federal policy continuity intact, limiting immediate implications for the Malaysian Ringgit (MYR).

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Johor result keeps policy continuity – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Barisan Nasional’s strong win in Johor reinforces UMNO’s political momentum but leaves federal policy continuity intact, limiting immediate implications for the Malaysian Ringgit (MYR).

item.title: British Pound Sterling buckles as Trump builds the Hormuz toll booth he swore would never exist
item.description: The British Pound Sterling is spending Monday learning the difference between a recovery and a reprieve.

item.title: Euro slides as Waller warning, Iran strikes lift US Dollar
item.description: The shared currency begins the week on a lower note, down 0.31% as risk aversion fueled flows towards the US Dollar amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. Also, hawkish comments by a Fed official underpinned US Treasury yields, suggesting markets expect the US central bank to raise rates.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Consolidation after sharper drop against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH fell more than expected to 6.7766 before rebounding, with the sharp decline seen stabilising and intraday consolidation likely between 6.7780 and 6.7920. For the next 1–3 weeks, they expect range trading between 6.7700 and 6.8100.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risks with CPI and Warsh in view – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong observe that USD/SGD has turned slightly softer, tracking Renminbi (RMB) gains as the Dollar consolidates. They see risks skewed to the downside, with support at 1.29 and 1.2840 and resistance at 1.2980.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar surges as Hormuz tensions send Oil to one-month high
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) surges toward 101.30, gaining around 0.3% as escalating tensions between the United States (US) and Iran boost safe-haven demand and drive energy prices sharply higher.

item.title: Taiwan: AI cycle and 2H outlook – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research, led by Ma Tieying, assesses Taiwan’s AI-driven expansion and its implications for the 2H26 outlook. The bank notes that AI remains central for Taiwan’s technology-oriented economy and that the AI supercycle is nearing a peak.

item.title: Malaysian Ringgit: Stable as BNM holds rates – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao and Moses Lim note that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) kept the OPR at 2.75% for a sixth straight meeting, maintaining a cautious tone on global risks. Growth is still expected within a 4–5% range, with inflation contained.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi holds below 200-day as bears target 0.5700
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar recoiled during Monday’s North American session, down 0.12%, as the Greenback posted gains versus most G8 FX currencies amid rising geopolitical tensions and hawkish comments from a Fed Governor. The NZD/USD trades at 0.5754, down from daily highs of 0.5789.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Stronger fix guides gradual RMB gains – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that USD/CNH dipped after a stronger USD/CNY fix below 6.80, the first such level since February 2023. They read this as policymakers being comfortable with further RMB appreciation while managing the pace.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG downtrend accelerates, eyes on $55.00
item.description: Silver price remains below $60.00 as the week begins, diving nearly 4% on Monday amid tensions in the Middle East. Hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller underpin the Greenback, which, according to the US Dollar Index (DXY), is up by over 0.28%.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as Hormuz tensions and policy concerns weigh
item.description: USD/JPY trades higher near 162.40 on Monday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) weakens amid escalating tensions between the United States (US) and Iran. The US Dollar (USD) remains supported by higher Oil prices and growing concerns that renewed energy pressure could keep global inflation elevated.
